artifacts.synopsis: RE Paul M. Wright filed a complaint against Eastern Carolina Presbytery regarding its response to a Reference from White Oak Presbyterian Church Session on a doctrinal issue. The SJC found the case judicially out of order because the Presbytery's action was advice only in response to a Reference for advice under BCO 41-1, and such advisory actions are not complainable under BCO 43. The Panel recommended the case be found out of order. Vote: 17 concurring, 1 dissenting (RE J. Howard Donahoe), 1 abstaining, 4 absent.

artifacts.synopsis: Herman Gunter III and Donald Monroe challenged their Session's refusal to approve them for examination as ruling elders based on its assessment of their theonomic views and alleged divisiveness. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that the Session could evaluate theological and character issues affecting eligibility for office and could exercise judgment for the church's peace and purity.

artifacts.synopsis: Bruce Nickoley and David Stephens complained against Southwest Presbytery's actions in withdrawing charges against two ruling elders, dissolving a pastoral relationship, and rescinding its suspension of a local church session. The SJC denied the complaint, affirming that the Presbytery correctly determined it lacked constitutional authority to suspend the session or act as a 'Session pro tem' without congregational consent, and that original jurisdiction over charges against ruling elders rested with the local session.

artifacts.synopsis: TE David Bowen complained against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's actions rescinding its 1988 decision and annulling the elections and ordinations of ruling elders and deacons at the Church of the Good Shepherd who took exception to infant baptism and limited atonement. The SJC sustained the complaint that ECP erred in rescinding a two-year-old action and annulling ordinations without due process under BCO 24-6, while also affirming that infant baptism and limited atonement are fundamentals of the system of doctrine for which no exceptions may be granted for church officers.

matches.evidence: BCO 24-1 applies fully to men with no prior official relationship to the church; for men already serving, lower courts determine which provisions apply at re-election.

artifacts.title: Congregational requirement of supermajority vote to elect church officers

matches.evidence: The PCA Constitution does not permit a congregation to require that candidates for church office receive more than a majority vote to be elected.
